problems.title: Both signs of a sum are possible
problems.question: xy=15,x²+y²=34. Find the least possible x+y.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: The squared sum is 34+30=64, so x+y=±8. Both are possible: (3,5) and (−3,−5) meet the data. The minimum is −8.

problems.title: Range of a negative square
problems.question: Find the range of y=−x²−4x−4.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: It is at most zero, reaching zero at x=−2, and has no lower bound.

problems.title: An unbounded integer solution set
problems.question: How many integer solutions has x²−8x+3≥0?
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: All x≤4−√13 or x≥4+√13 work. In particular, every integer x≤0 or x≥8 is a solution, so there are infinitely many.

problems.title: Recognize a right triangle from squared sides
problems.question: Find the area of a triangle with sides √11,√12,√23.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: The first two sides are perpendicular legs. Area=√11·√12/2=√132/2=√33.

problems.title: A bisector splits the opposite leg
problems.question: An acute-angle bisector of a right triangle divides the opposite leg into 4 and 5. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: The opposite leg is 9. Write hypotenuse=5t and adjacent leg=4t. Pythagoras gives 25t²=16t²+81, so t=3.
The legs are 9,12 and area=9×12/2=54.

problems.title: A linear expression dominates an absolute value
problems.question: Solve 5x+1≥|2x+1|.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: Require 5x+1≥2x+1, giving x≥0, and 5x+1≥−2x−1, giving x≥−2/7. Their intersection is x≥0.

problems.title: Range on a closed domain interval
problems.question: Find the range of x²+6x−2 for x∈[−4,0].
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: The vertex x=−3 is allowed and gives minimum −11. Endpoints give f(−4)=−10,f(0)=−2, so the maximum is −2. Continuity fills the interval.

problems.title: Which quadratics increase on the same interval?
problems.question: a(x)=−x²−4x+3,b(x)=x²−4x+31,c(x)=x²+4x+1,d(x)=−3x²−12x+13. Which two have matching increasing intervals?
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: Complete each square to identify its vertex and opening direction.
steps: a=−(x+2)²+7 and d=−3(x+2)²+25 both increase up to x=−2.
b=(x−2)²+27 increases after x=2, while c=(x+2)²−3 increases after x=−2. Thus a and d match.

problems.title: Circumradius from an isosceles height
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 6 and base altitude 4. Find circumradius.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: $R=abc/(4S)$; if base is b and height h, this gives $R=L^2/(2h)$.
steps: R=36/(2×4)=4.5. The base is positive since the half-base is √(36−16).

problems.title: Rhombus angle from diagonal halves
problems.question: A rhombus has diagonals 2a,2b. Find the sine of one of its angles.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: Thus sinθ=2ab/(a²+b²). Adjacent rhombus angles are supplementary and have the same sine.

problems.title: Factor a quadratic with radical roots
problems.question: Solve x²−(√2+1)x+√2<0.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: An upward-opening quadratic is negative strictly between its roots, giving 1<x<√2.

problems.title: A parabola visits all four quadrants
problems.question: A quadratic ax²+bx+c, a≠0, has points in every coordinate quadrant. What must hold for its discriminant D?
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: If D≤0, a nondegenerate quadratic never has both positive and negative values.
steps: Visiting all four quadrants requires some positive y values and some negative y values. By continuity the graph crosses the x-axis twice, so D>0.
The sign of a is not fixed: both upward and downward examples can visit all quadrants.

problems.title: When can an absolute-value equation have a root?
problems.question: Find all a such that 3a−2|2x+1|=6 has at least one real solution.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: An absolute value attains every nonnegative value and no negative value. Require 3a−6≥0, or a≥2. At a=2 the single root is x=−1/2.

problems.title: Sine of a supplementary angle
problems.question: A triangle has A=45°,B=30°,AB=√3+1. Find sin C.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: Angle addition gives sin75°=sin45°cos30°+cos45°sin30°=(√6+√2)/4=(√3+1)/(2√2).
The side length is unnecessary for this question.

problems.title: A ratio of circumradius to inradius
problems.question: A triangle has perimeter k, area 2k and side product 65k. Find R/r.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: R=65k/(8k)=65/8 and r=2k/(k/2)=4. Their ratio is 65/32.

problems.title: Vertex height from two roots and an intercept
problems.question: A parabola goes through (1,0),(3,0),(0,9). Find its vertex y coordinate.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: At x=0, 9=3a, so a=3. The symmetry axis is midway between roots, x=2. Then y=3×1×(−1)=−3.

problems.title: A vertex-form parabola’s intercept
problems.question: A parabola has vertex (−1,2) and passes through (1,18). Find its y-axis intercept.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: 18=4a+2 gives a=4. At x=0, y=4+2=6, so the intercept is (0,6).

problems.title: Minimize an isosceles side
problems.question: The base and base altitude of an isosceles triangle sum to 10. Find the minimum equal-side length.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: If base is b and height 10−b, then $L^2=b^2/4+(10-b)^2$.
steps: Complete the square: L²=(5/4)(b−8)²+20. Thus L≥√20=2√5.
Equality at b=8,height=2 gives a valid nondegenerate triangle.

problems.title: Two triangles from side-side-angle data
problems.question: AB=20,BC=15,cos A=4/5. Find the difference between the greatest and least possible areas.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: b²−32b+175=0 gives b=7 or 25. Both satisfy triangle inequalities. Since A is acute, sin A=3/5.
Area=(1/2)×20×b×3/5=6b, giving 42 and 150. Their difference is 108.

problems.title: Length scale and area units both matter
problems.question: Triangle 1 has sides a,b,c cm; Triangle 2 has sides a,b,c dm. Divide Triangle 2’s area measured in cm² by Triangle 1’s area measured in dm².
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: Lengths scale by 10, areas by 100; $1\text{ dm}^2=100\text{ cm}^2$.
steps: Let Triangle 1 area be S cm². Triangle 2 then has area 100S cm², while Triangle 1’s area is S/100 dm².
The requested numerical ratio is 100S/(S/100)=10000=10⁴.

problems.title: A weighted sum of squares with fixed sum
problems.question: a+b=15. Find the minimum of 2a²+b².
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: Substitute b=15−a and complete the square.
steps: 2a²+(15−a)²=3(a−5)²+150. The minimum 150 is attained at a=5,b=10.

problems.title: Count integer roots of a rational inequality
problems.question: Count integer x satisfying [(x²−3)(x²−5x+4)]/[(x+3)²(x²+2)]≤0.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: The denominator is positive except at excluded x=−3; factor the numerator as $(x-\sqrt3)(x+\sqrt3)(x-1)(x-4)$.
steps: The nonpositive intervals are [−√3,1] and [√3,4]. The denominator restriction does not remove any point in these intervals.
The integers are −1,0,1,2,3,4, a total of six.

problems.title: Two quadratic ranges must cover the real line
problems.question: For which a do ranges of f(x)=−x²+6x+2a−3 and g(x)=2x²−8x+a²+6 have union R?
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
steps: Their ranges are (−∞,2a+6] and [a²−2,∞). They cover R iff a²−2≤2a+6.
This is (a−4)(a+2)≤0, giving −2≤a≤4.

problems.title: Heron’s formula with tangent-length variables
problems.question: An incircle touches AB,BC,AC at M,N,K, with AM=a²,BN=b²,CK=c² and a,b,c>0. Find triangle area.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: Equal tangent lengths give sides $a^2+b^2,b^2+c^2,a^2+c^2$; Heron $S=\sqrt{s(s-u)(s-v)(s-w)}$.
steps: The semiperimeter is s=a²+b²+c². The other three Heron factors are c²,a²,b².
Thus S=abc√(a²+b²+c²), taking positive a,b,c.

problems.title: The side lengths contradict the diagonal angle
problems.question: A parallelogram has sides 1,3 and cosine 3/5 for the angle between its diagonals. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use an algebraic identity or geometric formula and check whether all the data can hold.
formulas: For side vectors u,v and diagonals p=u+v,q=u−v, $|p\cdot q|=||u|^2-|v|^2|=8$; $|p|^2+|q|^2=20$.
steps: AM–GM gives |p||q|≤10. Therefore the cosine of the smaller diagonal angle is at least 8/10=4/5. It cannot be 3/5.
Equivalently, forcing cosine 3/5 would give |p||q|=40/3 and sine 4/5, hence area=|p||q|sinθ/2=16/3, larger than the maximum side-product area 1×3=3.
No real parallelogram satisfies all the stated data.
problems.note: The printed measurements are inconsistent. Every listed numerical area also exceeds the maximum possible area 3, so none is valid.
